Family and Relationships: Different Fami.topic: Family and Relationships: Different Family Traditions
Family and Relationships: Different Fami.title: Our Special Family Traditions

scenes.title: What are family traditions?
narration: Have you ever wondered why your family celebrates special days in a unique way?
Every family has its own fun habits that make them feel close together.
These special habits are what we call family traditions.

scenes.title: Why do we have them?
narration: Traditions help us remember our history and the people who came before us.
They also bring joy and comfort to our daily lives.
When we do things together, we create happy memories that last forever.

scenes.title: An Indian family example
narration: Meet Aarav, whose family makes delicious homemade jalebis every Sunday morning.
Aarav helps his dad stir the batter while his mom fries them hot.
They all sit together on the balcony to eat and talk about their week.
This simple act is a tradition that keeps their family bond very strong.

scenes.title: Remember and think
narration: Traditions can be about food, festivals, games, or even how we greet elders.
They connect us to our culture and make every family special.
Think about it: What is one special tradition your family does every year?

Family and Relationships: Caring for Oth.topic: Family and Relationships: Caring for Others
Family and Relationships: Caring for Oth.title: Caring for Your Family

scenes.title: The Magic of Helping
narration: Have you ever seen your grandmother struggle to carry her heavy grocery bags from the market?
What can you do to make her day a little bit brighter and easier?
Caring for others is like planting a seed of love that grows every single day.

scenes.title: Ways to Show Love
narration: We show we care by listening when someone shares a story about their day.
You can also help by tidying up your toys after you finish playing.
Small acts like bringing a glass of water show you are thoughtful.
When we share our snacks or toys, it makes our family feel happy.

scenes.title: A Day with Rohan
narration: Rohan sees his sister struggling with her math homework at the kitchen table.
Instead of playing, he sits down and helps her solve a tricky problem.
His sister smiles, and their bond becomes even stronger because of his kindness.

scenes.title: Remembering to Care
narration: Caring means helping, listening, and sharing with the people we love most.
You become a hero in your own home every time you show kindness.
Think about it: who can you surprise with a kind act today?

Our Community: Rural and Urban Communiti.topic: Our Community: Rural and Urban Communities
Our Community: Rural and Urban Communiti.title: City Life or Village Life

scenes.title: Where do you live?
narration: Look around your home, do you see tall buildings or wide green fields?
I live in a busy city, but my cousin Kabir lives in a quiet village.
Why are these two places so different from each other?

scenes.title: Learning about Communities
narration: Urban areas are cities with many tall buildings, buses, and busy roads.
Rural areas are villages with open land, farms, and fewer people.
Both places have houses, schools, and markets for the people living there.

scenes.title: A Day in India
narration: In Mumbai, Priya takes a fast train to her crowded school.
In a Punjab village, Harpreet helps his father harvest wheat on the farm.
Priya buys snacks at a mall, while Harpreet buys vegetables at a weekly haat.

scenes.title: Wrapping it Up
narration: Cities have many buildings and people, while villages have farms and nature.
Every community helps us live, learn, and grow together in our country.
If you could visit a village or a city today, where would you go?

scenes.title: The Happy Home Puzzle
narration: Look around your home, do you see how much work your family does every single day?
Have you ever wondered why we all help each other with chores like cleaning and cooking?
Being part of a family means we are a team that works together.

scenes.title: What Are Responsibilities
narration: A responsibility is a job we do to help our family run smoothly.
When we do our part, it makes our home a happy and organized place.
Chores might seem small, but they show that we care about our loved ones.

scenes.title: A Day With Rohan
narration: Rohan helps his mother by setting the table with plates for dinner.
Then, he waters the tulsi plant in the balcony while his father cooks dal.
By tidying his toys, Rohan makes more space for everyone to relax together.
Everyone is happy because they finished their tasks as a team.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Remember, chores help our family and show we care for each other.
When everyone helps, we have more time to laugh and play games.
Think about it: what is one small job you can do today to surprise your family?

scenes.title: Meet Your Helpful Neighbors
narration: Have you ever wondered who keeps our neighborhood running smoothly every single day?
From the bread in your kitchen to the school bus, people work hard to help us.
Let us look at some of the important jobs right here in our town.

scenes.title: Learning About Important Jobs
narration: A baker wakes up early to bake fresh rotis and bread for our breakfast.
A shopkeeper sells us milk, rice, and pulses at the local corner store.
The postman delivers our letters and parcels all across the city streets.
Teachers at school help us learn new things and discover the world.

scenes.title: A Day With Rohan
narration: Rohan visits the vegetable seller, Mrs. Gupta, to buy fresh carrots with ten rupees.
Then, he sees the traffic police officer keeping the busy street crossing safe.
Finally, the doctor at the clinic checks his pulse to make sure he is healthy.

scenes.title: Thank You To Our Helpers
narration: Every job is special because it makes our lives easier and better.
We should always be kind and say thank you to people who help us.
Think about it, what job would you like to do when you grow up?

scenes.title: The Busy Neighborhood
narration: Have you noticed how many people help us in our neighborhood every single day?
From the park to the post office, who makes sure everything works smoothly?
Let's find out how community services keep our lives safe and happy.

scenes.title: Essential Services Defined
narration: Community services are jobs that help everyone living in the same area.
We pay for these with taxes, which are small amounts of money from everyone.
The government uses this money to hire workers and build important places.
These services make our daily lives much easier and safer.

scenes.title: A Day in Our Town
narration: Meet Arjun, he visits the local library to borrow books for his school project.
Later, a fire truck rushes past to keep the neighborhood safe from accidents.
Then, a sanitation worker clears the street to keep our town clean and healthy.
Finally, the doctor at the clinic helps his sister feel better.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Community services include schools, libraries, hospitals, and emergency helpers.
These helpers work together to keep our community clean, safe, and organized.
Think about it: What is one community service you use every single week?

scenes.title: Welcome to School
narration: Do you ever wonder why your school has so many special rooms?
Every school is a place where we learn, play, and make friends.
Let us look at the places that make our school work.

scenes.title: Learning and Growing
narration: The classroom is where we read books and learn about numbers.
The library is a quiet place filled with thousands of stories.
We visit the computer lab to learn about the digital world.

scenes.title: Playing and Staying Healthy
narration: At playtime, we run and jump in the big school playground.
We go to the canteen to buy a healthy snack with our rupees.
Our school clinic is there to help us feel better if we get hurt.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: From classrooms to playgrounds, every space has a special purpose.
We must keep these places clean and respect our school property.
Which part of your school is your favorite, and why do you like it?

scenes.title: The Busy Market Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered where your favorite fresh vegetables come from?
Today we are visiting the colorful local market near our school.
Let us see what makes a market such a busy place.

scenes.title: How a Market Works
narration: Markets are places where people sell things they have grown or made.
Buyers come with money to pick out exactly what they need.
Shopkeepers set up stalls and arrange their items neatly on shelves.
It is a big community effort to keep us fed and happy.

scenes.title: A Trip to the Shop
narration: Rohan goes to the market with fifty rupees in his pocket.
He chooses a bunch of shiny bananas for twenty rupees.
He gives the money to the shopkeeper and gets his change back.
Now he has healthy fruit and thirty rupees left for tomorrow.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Markets help us buy goods like food, clothes, and school supplies.
Remember, always be polite when you talk to the shopkeeper.
Think about it: what would you buy if you had ten rupees today?

scenes.title: Visiting The Busy Bank
narration: Have you ever seen your parents putting money into a safe place called a bank?
Why do we keep money there instead of just inside a piggy bank?
Let us find out how a bank helps us keep our money safe.

scenes.title: Keeping Our Money Safe
narration: A bank is a building that protects our paper money and metal coins.
We can open a special account to store our savings securely.
The bank staff helps us count and record every single rupee.

scenes.title: An Afternoon At The Bank
narration: Rohan goes to the bank with his mother to deposit five hundred rupees.
The teller writes the amount in Rohan's small bank passbook.
Now his money is safe and he can take it out later.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Banks are safe places to store money and keep it growing.
They help families manage their money for important things like school fees.
Think about it: If you had a hundred rupees, would you save it or spend it?

scenes.title: A Place That Helps
narration: Have you ever wondered who helps you feel better when you are sick?
When we need extra care, we visit a special place called a hospital.
Let us see who works inside to keep us healthy and strong.

scenes.title: The Hospital Team
narration: Doctors are experts who listen to our heart and check our health.
Nurses are very kind and help us take our medicine on time.
Receptionists help us find the right room when we first walk in.

scenes.title: A Check-up Visit
narration: Imagine Rohan visits the hospital for a routine check-up in Delhi.
First, the nurse weighs him and checks how tall he has grown.
Then, the doctor uses a stethoscope to listen to his happy heartbeat.
Rohan leaves with a sticker and a big smile because he is healthy.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Helpers
narration: Hospitals are important places filled with people who care for our community.
Doctors and nurses work hard every single day to keep us safe.
Think about it: What is one nice thing you could say to a doctor?

scenes.title: Sending A Special Letter
narration: Have you ever wondered how your birthday card reaches your friend in another city?
It all starts at the local post office in your neighborhood.
Let us follow the journey of a letter today.

scenes.title: Inside The Post Office
narration: First, you drop your letter into a big red post box.
A postal worker collects the mail and takes it inside the building.
Every letter gets a special ink stamp called a postmark.
This mark shows where and when the letter was posted.

scenes.title: A Letter To Chennai
narration: Imagine you are sending a letter from Delhi to your cousin in Chennai.
Your letter travels on a fast train or an airplane.
It arrives at the Chennai post office to be sorted by street.
Finally, the friendly postman puts the letter right in your cousin's mailbox.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Post offices collect, stamp, sort, and deliver our letters everywhere.
They help us stay connected with family and friends across India.
Think about it: what would you write in a letter to a friend today?

scenes.title: Meeting a Friendly Helper
narration: Have you seen a police station while walking to your school in India?
It is a special place where officers work hard to keep us safe.
Have you ever wondered what exactly happens inside those walls?

scenes.title: What Police Officers Do
narration: Police officers help people who are in trouble or need some advice.
They patrol the streets in jeeps to make sure rules are followed.
They also help find lost things or help children who get separated.
They work day and night so that our neighborhoods stay peaceful.

scenes.title: A Day at the Station
narration: Imagine Rohan loses his bag at the busy Delhi local market.
Rohan and his father go to the nearest police station for help.
An officer listens carefully and writes down the details in a book.
Soon, the officers use their network to find the lost bag safely.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Helpers
narration: Police stations keep our community safe and follow the law.
Remember, you can always ask a police officer for help if needed.
Think about it: Why is it important for us to follow rules?

scenes.title: The Daily Meal Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered where your yummy dal and rice come from?
It all starts far away in big, green fields.
Let's meet the amazing farmers who work hard every day.

scenes.title: How Farmers Grow Food
narration: First, the farmer prepares the soil to make it soft and healthy.
Then, they carefully sow tiny seeds into the earth.
The farmer adds water and sunshine to help the plants grow tall.
Finally, when the crops are ready, it is time for the harvest.

scenes.title: Example: Paddy Fields
narration: In places like Punjab or West Bengal, farmers grow rice plants.
They stand in water to plant the green rice stalks.
After months of care, the golden grains are ready for us.
The rice is packed into bags and sent to our local market.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflection
narration: Farmers work hard to plant, grow, and harvest our food.
Without them, we would not have delicious meals on our plates.
Think about it: what is your favorite vegetable grown by a farmer?

scenes.title: The Amazing World Around Us
narration: Have you ever wondered how a tall bridge stays up over a river?
Or how your school bus engine starts every single morning?
These things don't just appear; they are designed by clever people called engineers!

scenes.title: How Engineers Solve Problems
narration: Engineers are like super-solvers who use science and math to build cool things.
First, they think of a plan and draw it out on paper.
Then, they test their ideas to make sure everything is safe and strong.
If something breaks, they don't give up; they fix it and try again!

scenes.title: Building a Real Bridge
narration: Let us see how Arjun the engineer helps build a bridge over a canal.
He picks strong materials like steel and heavy concrete.
He calculates how much weight the bridge can hold safely.
Finally, the bridge is finished, and cars can cross it safely!

scenes.title: Engineers Change the World
narration: Engineers build our roads, our tall buildings, and even our computers.
They work hard to make our lives safer, faster, and much more fun.
Think about it: if you could build one new invention, what would it be?

scenes.title: Meeting Our Classroom Teacher
narration: Have you ever wondered how your teacher knows so much about everything?
Every morning at school, we see them ready to help us learn.
Teachers are special people who spend their days guiding us to grow.

scenes.title: What Do Teachers Actually Do?
narration: Teachers plan fun lessons to help us understand numbers and stories.
They show us how to write, read, and solve tricky math problems.
They also teach us how to be kind friends to our classmates.

scenes.title: A Day With Ms. Anjali
narration: Let us look at Ms. Anjali, a teacher in a school in Delhi.
First, she writes today's big science project on the green board.
Next, she walks around to help little Rahul with his drawing.
Finally, she cheers for everyone when they finish their work.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Teachers work hard to share knowledge and help us become our best.
They make our classrooms a safe place to ask questions.
What is one thing you learned today that made you smile?

scenes.title: The Friendly Neighborhood Shop
narration: Have you ever wondered how your favorite snacks get to your kitchen shelf?
When you visit a shop, you meet a very busy and helpful person.
Let us learn how our local shopkeeper helps the whole neighborhood.

scenes.title: What Does A Shopkeeper Do?
narration: A shopkeeper orders goods from big markets to keep shelves full.
They organize items neatly so you can find your pencil or soap.
They also help us by selling small amounts of things we need.

scenes.title: Buying Milk at the Shop
narration: Imagine you go to Mr. Gupta's shop to buy a packet of milk.
You pick the milk and bring it to the counter.
Mr. Gupta checks the price and you pay him 30 rupees.
He gives you the milk and a friendly smile too.

scenes.title: Our Helpful Community Friends
narration: Shopkeepers work hard to make sure we have food and supplies every day.
Without them, we would have to travel very far for everything.
Think about it: What is the most important thing you bought from a shop today?

scenes.title: Meeting a Local Doctor
narration: Have you ever visited Dr. Sharma at the clinic when you felt unwell?
She helps us feel better when we have a cough or a fever.
Have you ever wondered how doctors learn to fix our ouchies?

scenes.title: What Doctors Do
narration: Doctors study very hard to understand how our amazing bodies work.
They listen to our heartbeat using a cool tool called a stethoscope.
They check our eyes, ears, and throat to see what is wrong.
Then, they give us the right medicine to help us heal.

scenes.title: A Day at the Clinic
narration: Imagine little Rohan has a tummy ache after eating too many spicy samosas.
Dr. Sharma gently presses his tummy to find the sore spot.
She tells Rohan to drink lots of water and rest well.
Rohan feels much happier knowing he will be fine soon.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Heroes
narration: Doctors are important helpers who keep our whole community strong.
They work in hospitals and clinics to take care of everyone.
Think about it: What is one nice thing you could say to a doctor next time you see one?

Transport and Communication: Types of Tr.topic: Transport and Communication: Types of Transport
Transport and Communication: Types of Tr.title: How We Move Around India

scenes.title: The Big Question
narration: Have you ever wondered how Rohan gets to school or how your mangoes reach the market?
We use many different types of transport to move people and things everywhere.
Let us learn about land, water, and air travel together!

scenes.title: Travel on Land
narration: Land transport is the most common way to travel in our cities and villages.
Bicycles and auto-rickshaws are perfect for short trips inside your busy neighborhood.
For long distances, we use big buses or fast trains like the Vande Bharat.
Trains are great because they carry many people across our huge country.

scenes.title: Water and Air
narration: Do you live near a river? People use boats and ferries to cross the water.
Airplanes are the fastest way to travel if you need to go very far away.
Imagine flying from Delhi to Kochi in just a few hours instead of days!

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: We use land vehicles, boats for water, and airplanes to fly high.
Each transport type helps us reach our friends, family, and schools every single day.
Think about it: If you could travel anywhere tomorrow, would you go by train or plane?

scenes.title: Who Makes Your Things
narration: Look at the colorful clay pot on your kitchen table.
Have you ever wondered how it was made?
It was created by a talented person called an artisan.

scenes.title: What Do Artisans Do
narration: Artisans are skilled workers who make things by hand.
They use special tools to turn simple materials into art.
They spend years practicing to get their work just right.

scenes.title: The Weaver at Work
narration: Let us visit a weaver in a village in India.
First, the weaver gathers soft, colorful cotton threads.
Then, they move the loom back and forth to weave fabric.
Finally, a beautiful saree is ready to be worn.

scenes.title: Why Artisans Are Special
narration: Artisans bring beauty and culture to our daily lives.
Remember, every handmade item tells a special story.
Think about it: What is one handmade thing in your house?

scenes.title: The Big Red Bus
narration: Have you ever seen a big bus full of people in your city?
Why do so many people ride the bus instead of driving cars?
Let us find out how public transport helps us move around India.

scenes.title: Sharing The Ride
narration: Public transport means vehicles that anyone can pay a small ticket price to ride.
Buses, local trains, and the Metro are all ways we share our travel.
By sharing, we use less fuel and keep our air cleaner for everyone.

scenes.title: A Trip to School
narration: Aarav walks to the bus stop with his school bag.
He pays ten rupees and finds a seat next to his friend.
The bus driver takes them safely through the busy market streets.
Aarav arrives at school on time and ready to learn.

scenes.title: Summing It Up
narration: Public transport is shared, cheap, and good for our environment.
Remember to always queue nicely and be polite to others on board.
Think about it: What would your neighborhood look like if everyone drove their own car?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Talking
narration: Have you ever wondered how you talk to Grandma far away in Chennai?
We use a telephone to send our voice across many kilometers.
It is like a magic bridge for our voices.

scenes.title: How the Sound Travels
narration: When you speak, your voice turns into tiny electrical signals.
These signals travel very fast through wires or through the air.
Then, the other phone turns those signals back into sound.

scenes.title: A Call to Grandma
narration: Aarav dials his grandmother's number on his mobile phone.
The signal zips through invisible waves to reach her home.
Grandma hears Aarav say hello and smiles happily.

scenes.title: Key Points to Remember
narration: Telephones help us talk to people far away instantly.
Our voice travels as signals through wires or air.
Think about it: How did people send messages before phones?

scenes.title: Writing a Surprise Letter
narration: Have you ever sent a surprise letter to your friend in another city?
How does a piece of paper travel so far to reach someone?
Let us follow the journey of a letter from Delhi to Chennai.

scenes.title: The Post Office Journey
narration: First, you drop your letter into the red post box at the corner.
A postman collects it and takes it to the local post office.
Workers sort the letters by the address pin code written on them.
Each letter is stamped to show where it started its long trip.

scenes.title: Traveling Across India
narration: The letters are put into big bags and loaded onto a fast train.
The train speeds across India to reach the city of Chennai.
At the Chennai post office, another postman gets your letter.
He carries it safely to your friend’s house in his bag.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up Our Trip
narration: Post offices help us share news and love with people far away.
Remember, the pin code and address must be written clearly.
Think about it: who would you like to write a letter to today?

scenes.title: The Magic Screen
narration: Have you ever wondered how your tablet shows your favorite cartoon instantly?
It happens because of a super fast network called the internet.
Let us see how it connects our homes to the whole world.

scenes.title: Invisible Web of Wires
narration: The internet is like a giant spider web of cables.
These long wires run deep under the ground and even under oceans.
Data travels through these wires as tiny pulses of light.
Finally, the signal reaches your home router to give you Wi-Fi.

scenes.title: Sending a Digital Letter
narration: Imagine you want to send a photo of a yummy Dosa to a friend.
Your device breaks the photo into tiny digital pieces.
These pieces travel through wires to your friend's phone very fast.
The friend's phone puts the pieces back together to show the photo.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up
narration: The internet uses wires and light to share information globally.
It connects our family, friends, and schools across India and beyond.
Think about it: what is the most fun thing you have ever learned online?

Maps and Directions: Near and Far.topic: Maps and Directions: Near and Far
Maps and Directions: Near and Far.title: Finding Our Way Around

scenes.title: Where are things?
narration: Have you ever wondered how to find your way to the park?
We use maps to see where places are.
Maps show us if a place is near or far.

scenes.title: Understanding Directions
narration: We use directions like left, right, and straight.
Near means you can walk there quickly.
Far means you need a bus or a train.

scenes.title: An Afternoon in Delhi
narration: Let's look at a map of a neighborhood in Delhi.
Your house is near the vegetable market.
The big India Gate is far away.
You walk to the market but drive to the gate.

scenes.title: Time to Remember
narration: Maps help us find our way home.
Near is close and far needs a ride.
Think about it: what is one place near your school?

Maps and Directions: North, South, East,.topic: Maps and Directions: North, South, East, West
Maps and Directions: North, South, East,.title: Finding Our Way With Maps

scenes.title: Which Way Do We Go
narration: Have you ever been lost in a big market in Delhi?
How do we know which way to turn to get home?
Today we will learn how maps help us find our way.

scenes.title: The Four Main Directions
narration: The sun rises every morning in the East.
If you point your right hand to the East, the West is on your left.
North is always in front of you, and South is behind you.
These are the four main directions we use to travel.

scenes.title: Reading a Map of India
narration: Look at a map of India to find your state.
Kashmir is way up North, near the high mountains.
Kanyakumari is way down South, where the ocean meets the land.
Maps use symbols to show us exactly where cities are located.

scenes.title: Time to Recap
narration: Remember, maps help us find places using North, South, East, and West.
The sun always gives us a clue by rising in the East.
Think about it: If you face the rising sun, what direction is behind you?

Maps and Directions: Left and Right.topic: Maps and Directions: Left and Right
Maps and Directions: Left and Right.title: Finding Our Way Around

scenes.title: Where are we going
narration: Have you ever been lost in a big park or a busy market?
Rohan is trying to find his way to the school gate.
How can we tell him which way to turn?

scenes.title: Learning Left and Right
narration: Look at your own two hands right now.
Your right hand is the one you usually use to write.
Your other hand is your left hand.
Imagine holding a cricket bat or a spoon to know which is which.

scenes.title: Using a Map
narration: Rohan sees a simple map of his neighborhood.
To reach the park, he must turn right at the red building.
Then he turns left at the big banyan tree.
Following the map helps him arrive safely!

scenes.title: Summary and Thinking
narration: Remember, your right hand helps you find your way.
Maps use symbols to show us where to go.
Think about it: Can you draw a map from your front door to your kitchen?

scenes.title: Where are we going
narration: Have you ever wondered how to find your way to a friend's house?
Today, we will learn how to read a simple map.
A map is a drawing that shows us where places are.

scenes.title: Parts of a map
narration: Look for the compass rose that shows North, South, East, and West.
The map key explains what the tiny symbols mean.
Blue lines on a map often show us a river.
Black lines usually show the roads we walk on.

scenes.title: A trip in Delhi
narration: Let us look at a map of a park in Delhi.
First, find the gate on the map near the swings.
Follow the path North to reach the big water fountain.
Turn East to find the ice cream stall.

scenes.title: Reviewing what we learned
narration: Maps use symbols and a compass to show directions.
Always check the key to understand the map drawing.
Think about it, what would you draw to represent your school?

scenes.title: A Messy Park
narration: Look at this park filled with candy wrappers and plastic bottles.
Have you ever wondered why we must keep our surroundings clean?
Let us learn how a clean home makes a happy world.

scenes.title: Why Clean Matters
narration: Germs love to hide in piles of garbage and dirt.
Dirty places can make us feel sick and sneeze a lot.
But clean streets help us stay healthy and strong.
We must pick up trash to keep our air fresh.

scenes.title: Cleaning Up Together
narration: Rohan sees an empty juice box on the ground.
He picks it up and puts it in the blue bin.
Now the park looks beautiful for everyone to play.

scenes.title: Recap and Thinking
narration: Remember to throw trash in the bin, not the floor.
Clean places stop germs and keep our earth smiling.
Think about it, what can you clean in your room today?

scenes.title: The Hidden Secret Map
narration: Have you ever wondered how a map fits a whole city on one piece of paper?
Look at this map of Ananya's neighborhood in Delhi.
How do we know where the park or the school is without getting lost?

scenes.title: What Are Map Symbols
narration: Maps use tiny pictures called symbols to show real things.
A symbol is like a shortcut for our eyes.
Instead of drawing a whole tree, we use a simple green circle.
These symbols help us read maps quickly and easily.

scenes.title: Ananya's Map Adventure
narration: Ananya wants to walk from her house to the ice cream shop.
She spots a blue wavy line symbol for the Yamuna river.
She sees a red cross symbol showing the local hospital.
Finally, she finds the triangle symbol for the ice cream shop.

scenes.title: Mapping It All Out
narration: Symbols stand for real places like parks, rivers, and schools.
Always check the map key to see what each symbol means.
Think about it: What symbol would you draw for your own house?

scenes.title: The Trash Mystery
narration: Look at your dustbin after lunch, where does all that trash go?
When we throw things away, they do not just disappear forever.
Let us learn how to keep our beautiful India clean and green.

scenes.title: Sorting Our Waste
narration: First, we separate wet waste like leftover fruit peels and food.
Next, we put dry waste like paper, plastic, and glass together.
Wet waste turns into soil to help our garden plants grow.
Dry waste goes to factories to be made into new things.

scenes.title: Example at Home
narration: Rohan ate an orange and put the peel in the green bin.
Then he rinsed his empty milk carton and put it in the blue bin.
By sorting, Rohan stops the trash from hurting our local park.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Remember, wet waste helps plants and dry waste becomes new treasures.
Sorting your trash is a big help to Mother Earth.
Think about it: what is one thing you can recycle today?

scenes.title: A Look Around India
narration: Have you noticed the beautiful peacock dancing in the park?
India has special symbols that make our country unique.
Do you know why we chose these specific ones?

scenes.title: Learning Our National Icons
narration: Our national flower is the lovely pink lotus.
The Bengal Tiger is our strong national animal.
The majestic Banyan tree is our national tree.
These represent the nature of our vast land.

scenes.title: The Mango and The River
narration: Think of a yummy, sweet yellow mango in summer.
It is our favorite fruit from the orchard.
Then there is the long and holy River Ganga.
It flows from the Himalayas to the sea.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Symbols
narration: We have symbols for our birds, trees, and rivers.
These help us remember the beauty of India.
Think about it: which national symbol is your favorite?

scenes.title: Our Big Beautiful Country
narration: Have you ever traveled on a train across our giant country, India?
India is so big that we divide it into smaller parts called states.
Each state has a special city that acts as its main office, called a capital.

scenes.title: Understanding States and Capitals
narration: Think of a state like a room in your house, and the capital is the main room.
The capital city is where the state leaders work to help everyone.
India has twenty-eight states, and each one has its own unique capital city.

scenes.title: A Visit to Maharashtra
narration: Let us look at the state of Maharashtra, famous for its yummy vada pav.
The capital city of Maharashtra is the busy and bright city of Mumbai.
Leaders meet in Mumbai to make plans for the people of Maharashtra.

scenes.title: Quick Recap and Think
narration: States are parts of India, and capitals are the main cities where leaders work.
Remember, every state in our country has its own special capital city.
Can you find out the name of the capital city of your own state?

scenes.title: The Wonder of India
narration: Have you ever traveled to see a big, beautiful building or a tall mountain?
Our country, India, is filled with many special places to visit.
Let's explore some famous landmarks together today!

scenes.title: Famous Landmarks
narration: In Agra, the Taj Mahal shines bright white like a jewel.
In Delhi, the India Gate stands tall to honor brave soldiers.
These places tell us stories about our history.
They help us remember the past in a fun way.

scenes.title: Natural Beauty
narration: Now, let's look at the cool mountains in the North.
The Himalayas are home to beautiful snowy peaks.
In the South, we find warm, sunny beaches with blue water.
India has everything from tall mountains to sandy shores.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: We learned about historic buildings and amazing nature.
India is a big country with so much to see.
Think about it: which place would you want to visit first?

Our Environment: Natural and Human-made.topic: Our Environment: Natural and Human-made Things
Our Environment: Natural and Human-made.title: Natural or Human-Made?

scenes.title: Spotting Things Around Us
narration: Look around your room, what do you see?
Some things are made by nature, like trees.
Other things are made by people, like your toys.

scenes.title: Understanding Natural Things
narration: Nature creates things that grow on their own.
Like the sun, the clouds, and the river Ganges.
They do not need people to build them.
They are here for us to enjoy and protect.

scenes.title: Understanding Human-Made Things
narration: People use materials to build new things.
Like your school bag, a bicycle, or a table.
We use wood, metal, or plastic to make them.
Think of a yummy samosa made in a kitchen.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Natural things are from nature, not made by us.
Human-made things are created by people.
Now, can you find one natural and one human-made thing in your park?

scenes.title: What Makes India Special?
narration: Have you noticed how many different languages your friends speak?
From spicy dosas to sweet rasgullas, our food is so different everywhere!
Why is India like a giant, beautiful patchwork quilt?

scenes.title: Our Different Ways
narration: People in India celebrate many happy festivals like Diwali, Eid, and Christmas.
We wear colorful clothes like sarees, kurtas, and turbans depending on where we live.
Even our houses look different, from snowy mountains to sunny beaches.
These differences are what make our country so exciting and fun.

scenes.title: A Day in India
narration: Imagine Priya in Kerala eating rice on a banana leaf.
Think of Kabir in Punjab dancing to the beat of a dhol.
Even though they are far apart, they are both proud Indians.

scenes.title: The Big Picture
narration: We have many languages, foods, and clothes, but we are one big family.
Respecting our differences helps India stay strong and happy.
What is your favorite festival that you share with your friends?
